sections.text: Part IV - Recipients and processors

I understand Acme may share my personal data with: (i) cloud hosting providers (Amazon Web Services India); (ii) payment processors (Razorpay Software Pvt. Ltd.); (iii) KYC verification partners; (iv) email and SMS delivery services; and (v) professional advisers bound by confidentiality. A current list is published at https://www.acmedigital.in/subprocessors. Acme remains accountable as Data Fiduciary.
Part V - Retention and erasure

Personal data will be retained only for the period necessary to fulfil each consented purpose, as set out in Acme's Data Retention Policy (typically: account data for relationship duration plus three years; marketing preferences until withdrawal plus three years for proof of consent). Thereafter data is securely erased or irreversibly anonymised unless law requires longer retention.
Part VI - Rights of the Data Principal
Right of access (Section 11): I may request a summary of my personal data being processed and the identities of fiduciaries and processors with whom it has been shared.
Right of correction and erasure (Section 12): I may request correction of inaccurate data or erasure when retention is no longer necessary.
Right of grievance redressal (Section 13): I may contact the Grievance Officer below before approaching the Data Protection Board of India.
Right of nomination (Section 14): I may nominate another individual to exercise my rights in the event of my death or incapacity.
Grievance Officer: Priya Sharma · grievance@acmedigital.in · +91 22 4890 2100 · Response within timelines prescribed under the DPDP Rules, 2025.
Part VII - Withdrawal of consent

I may withdraw any optional consent at any time by: (a) toggling preferences in my Acme account settings; (b) emailing privacy@acmedigital.in; or (c) submitting the Consent Withdrawal Request form at https://www.acmedigital.in/privacy/withdraw. Withdrawal is as easy as giving consent. Withdrawal does not affect lawfulness of processing before withdrawal or processing under another lawful basis.
Part VIII - Declaration

I confirm that: (i) I am at least 18 years of age, or I am the parent/legal guardian providing verifiable consent on behalf of a child; (ii) the information I have provided is accurate; (iii) I have read and understood this form and the Privacy Policy; and (iv) I freely give the consents I have ticked above.

sections.text: 2. Actions requested
With immediate effect upon receipt of this notice, I request that Acme:

Remove me from all marketing distribution lists and disable non-essential cookies linked to my account within seventy-two (72) hours.

3. Acknowledgement of limitations

I understand that: (a) withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing conducted on the basis of consent before its withdrawal; (b) Acme may continue to process my data where another lawful basis applies, including for core account services, legal compliance, or legitimate uses under Section 7; and (c) withdrawal of consent for core services may require closure of my account where processing is necessary for that service.

Acme Digital Solutions Private Limited ("Acme Digital", "Company", "we", "us", "our"), CIN U72900MH2019PTC328417, is the Data Fiduciary for personal data processed through https://www.acmedigital.in, the Acme mobile application and associated business channels.

This Privacy Policy constitutes the itemised notice required under Section 5 of the Act. It describes the categories of personal data collected, the purposes of processing, the rights available to Data Principals and the mechanism for grievance redressal.
1. Introduction and scope

This Policy applies to personal data collected through the Platform, at industry events, through sales and support channels, and from business partners. It does not apply to anonymised data or third-party websites governed by separate privacy notices.
2. Definitions and interpretation

items: "Personal data" means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data (Section 2(t), DPDP Act).
"Processing" means an automated operation or series of operations performed on digital personal data (Section 2(v)).
"Data Principal" means the individual to whom the personal data relates (Section 2(j)).
"Data Fiduciary" means any person who alone or in conjunction with others determines the purpose and means of processing (Section 2(i)).
"Data Processor" means any person who processes personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary (Section 2(k)).

sections.text: 3. Contact details and Grievance Officer

sections.text: 4. Scope

This policy applies to personal data we collect through the Platform, at industry events, through our sales and support channels, and from business partners. It does not apply to anonymised or non-personal data, or to third-party websites linked from our Platform (those have their own policies).
5. Personal data we collect
5.1 Data you provide directly

items: Registration data: name, work email, phone, company name, designation, password (hashed)
KYC / business verification: PAN, GSTIN, certificate of incorporation, authorised signatory ID
Billing: billing address, bank account or UPI details for settlements

sections.text: 5.2 Data collected automatically

items: Device and browser: IP address, operating system, browser type, device identifiers
Usage logs: pages viewed, features used, clickstream, crash reports, session duration

Cookies and similar technologies - see our Cookie Policy

sections.text: 5.3 Data from third parties

Publicly available business registries for KYB checks

sections.text: 6. Purposes and lawful bases
7. Consent management

Where we rely on consent, it is obtained through unticked checkboxes, granular cookie banners, or signed consent forms - never through pre-ticked boxes or dark patterns. You may withdraw consent at any time via account settings or privacy@acmedigital.in. Withdrawal is as easy as giving consent.
8. Sharing and Data Processors
We share personal data only with processors who provide services on our documented instructions, including:

rows: Amazon Web Services India Pvt. Ltd.

sections.text: Each processor is bound by a Data Processing Agreement requiring Rule 6 security safeguards. We may also disclose data to courts, regulators, or law enforcement when required by applicable law.
9. Cross-border transfers (Section 16)

Where personal data is transferred outside India (e.g. to Acme Digital Pte. Ltd., our Singapore affiliate, for group financial consolidation), we ensure the destination country is not on any restricted list notified under Section 16(1) and implement contractual safeguards requiring protection equivalent to the DPDP Rules. Details are available on request.
10. Retention

We retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes in Section 6. Indicative periods: active account data - duration of relationship; post-closure account data - 3 years; GST and tax records - 8 years; support tickets - 24 months; marketing consent logs - 3 years after withdrawal; security logs - minimum 12 months (Rule 8(3)). See our Data Retention Policy for the full schedule.
11. Security safeguards (Rule 6)

items: AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit for sensitive data
Role-based access control, MFA for administrative access, quarterly access reviews
ISO 27001-aligned information security management system (certification in progress)
Annual penetration testing and vulnerability remediation SLAs
Employee background checks and mandatory data protection training
Incident response plan with 24×7 security operations monitoring

sections.text: 12. Your rights
Request a summary of your personal data, processing purposes, and sharing with other fiduciaries/processors.
Request correction of inaccurate data or erasure when no longer necessary or upon consent withdrawal.
Lodge a complaint with our Grievance Officer. If unsatisfied, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India.
Nominate another individual to exercise your rights in the event of death or incapacity.
Withdraw consent for consent-based processing at any time without affecting prior lawful processing.
Submit requests via https://www.acmedigital.in/privacy/rights-request or email grievance@acmedigital.in. We respond within statutory timelines after identity verification.
13. Children's personal data (Section 9)

The Platform is intended for business users aged 18 and above. We do not knowingly process children's personal data. We do not track, monitor behaviourally advertise to, or target children. Where verifiable parental consent is required, we obtain it before processing.
14. Automated decision-making

We use automated fraud-scoring to protect transactions. This does not produce legal or similarly significant effects without human review. You may request explanation of automated decisions affecting you by contacting privacy@acmedigital.in.
15. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy to reflect legal, technical or business changes. Material changes will be notified by email or prominent Platform notice at least fifteen (15) days before taking effect. The "Last updated" date indicates the current version.
16. Governing law
This policy is governed by the laws of India. Courts at Mumbai, Maharashtra shall have exclusive jurisdiction subject to your right to approach the Data Protection Board.

1. Policy objective

This policy implements the storage limitation duty under Section 8(5) of the DPDP Act: personal data shall not be retained beyond the period necessary to satisfy the purpose for which it was collected. It applies to all business units of Acme Digital Solutions Private Limited.
2. Retention schedule
3. Erasure procedure
Trigger identified - retention period expiry, erasure request, consent withdrawal, or purpose fulfilment.
Business owner confirms no legal hold, litigation or regulatory investigation prevents deletion.
IT executes deletion from production systems; ticket logged in Jira project ACME-PRIV.
Processors instructed to delete copies; confirmation received within 15 business days.
Backups containing deleted data roll off within 30 days (90 days for disaster-recovery tapes).
Grievance Officer confirms erasure to Data Principal where applicable.
4. Exceptions

Data may be retained beyond standard periods where necessary for: compliance with law; establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims; regulatory examination; or anonymised statistical analysis that cannot re-identify individuals. Extensions require written approval from Legal and the Data Protection Lead.

1. Policy statement

Acme Digital Solutions Private Limited is committed to protecting personal data in accordance with the DPDP Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025. This policy binds all employees, contractors, interns and third-party processors handling personal data on Acme's behalf.
2. Governance structure

rows: Ultimate accountability for data protection compliance
Resources and tone from the top
Day-to-day compliance, RoPA, DPIA, Board liaison

sections.text: 3. Data protection principles

items: Lawfulness, fairness and transparency in all processing
Purpose limitation - collect for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes
Data minimisation - adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary
Accuracy - keep personal data correct and up to date
Storage limitation - retain only as long as necessary
Integrity and confidentiality - appropriate security against unauthorised processing
Accountability - demonstrate compliance through documentation and audit

sections.text: 4. Lawful processing framework
Must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with clear affirmative action. Consent requests presented in plain language in English and Hindi.
Documented in RoPA before reliance - includes voluntary provision, state functions, employment, medical emergency and public interest as applicable.
No processing of children's data for tracking/behavioural advertising; no processing contrary to law; no denial of legal rights.
5. Notice requirements (Section 5)

Every collection point displays or links to a compliant privacy notice covering: fiduciary identity, personal data collected, purpose, grievance mechanism, and manner of exercising rights. Material changes communicated 15 days in advance.
6. Security safeguards (Rule 6)

items: Information Security Policy aligned to ISO 27001 controls
Encryption, access management, network security, endpoint protection
Secure SDLC with privacy review for new features processing personal data
Annual penetration test and continuous vulnerability scanning
Physical security at Mumbai office and data centre colocation

sections.text: 7. Processor management
No processor engaged without signed DPA, security assessment and RoPA entry. Sub-processors require prior approval. High-risk vendors subject to on-site or SOC 2 audit review annually.
8. Data Principal rights
All rights requests routed to grievance@acmedigital.in. Identity verification mandatory. Response within DPDP Rules timelines. Register maintained for 3 years.
9. Breach management (Rule 7)

All staff must report suspected breaches within 1 hour to security@acmedigital.in. Breach Response Playbook activated. Board notification within 72 hours where required. Post-incident review mandatory.
10. Training
Mandatory induction training within 14 days of joining; annual refresher; specialised training for Engineering, HR, Marketing and Customer Support. Completion tracked in LMS.
11. Significant Data Fiduciary obligations

If Acme is notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary under Section 10: appoint independent Data Protection Officer, conduct periodic DPIA, appoint India-based consent manager if applicable, and comply with additional audit requirements.
12. Disciplinary action
Violation of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination, without prejudice to penalties under the DPDP Act Schedule and civil or criminal liability.

Assessment reference: ACME-DPIA-2026-003 · Processing activity: AI customer support chatbot
1. Processing description

Acme is deploying an AI-powered customer support chatbot ("Acme Assist") on the Platform to handle tier-1 support queries. The chatbot uses large language model APIs hosted by Amazon Bedrock (Mumbai region) to generate responses based on Acme's knowledge base and the customer's account context.
2. Data categories and scale
3. Necessity and proportionality

Tier-1 queries (password reset, invoice download, status checks) represent 62% of support volume. Automating these reduces median response time from 4 hours to 90 seconds. Alternatives considered: expanded FAQ only (insufficient for personalised queries); offshore human agents (higher cost, same data exposure). Data minimisation: chatbot receives only fields needed per query type; full PAN/card numbers never passed to the model.
4. Risk assessment

rows: Prompt injection exposing other users' data
Bedrock DPA, encryption, no training on Acme data
Bias in responses to regional users

sections.text: 5. Mitigations implemented

items: Privacy notice updated to disclose AI support processing
Opt-out to human agent available in every chat session
PII redaction layer before prompts sent to model
SOC 2 audit of Bedrock configuration
Quarterly review of conversation samples for quality and privacy

sections.text: THIS DATA PROCESSING AGREEMENT ("Agreement") is executed on 01 April 2026 and forms an integral part of the Master Cloud Services Agreement dated 15 January 2024 between Acme Digital Solutions Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at Unit 402, Peninsula Business Park, Senapati Bapat Marg, Lower Parel, Mumbai 400013, Maharashtra, India ("Data Fiduciary") and CloudHost Technologies India Private Limited, having its registered office at Embassy Tech Village, Bengaluru 560103 ("Data Processor").
Recitals
The Data Fiduciary acts as a Data Fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and engages the Data Processor to provide managed cloud hosting services for the Acme Platform.
The parties wish to set out their respective rights and obligations regarding the processing of Personal Data in compliance with the Act and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025.
In the event of any inconsistency between this Agreement and the Master Cloud Services Agreement on matters of data protection, this Agreement shall prevail.
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows:
1. Definitions and interpretation
"Act" means the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
"Rules" means the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025.
"Personal Data" has the meaning in Section 2(t) of the Act.
"Processing", "Data Principal", "Data Fiduciary" and "Data Processor" have the meanings in the Act.
"Sub-processor" means any processor engaged by the Data Processor.
"Personal Data Breach" means unauthorised processing or disclosure of personal data.
2. Scope and duration
Processor shall process Personal Data solely to provide managed cloud hosting services for the Acme Platform as described in Annex A.
Processing continues for the term of the Master Agreement and any wind-down period not exceeding ninety (90) days.
3. Processor obligations
Process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Fiduciary, including with regard to cross-border transfers.
Ensure persons authorised to process are bound by written confidentiality obligations.
Implement technical and organisational measures in Annex B, consistent with Rule 6.
Not engage Sub-processors without Fiduciary's prior written authorisation per Annex C.
Assist Fiduciary in responding to Data Principal rights requests within fifteen (15) business days.
Delete or return all Personal Data within thirty (30) days of termination and certify deletion.
Make available information necessary to demonstrate compliance and permit audits per Clause 8.
Notify Fiduciary within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach.
4. Fiduciary obligations
Fiduciary warrants it has a lawful basis for processing and has provided compliant notices to Data Principals.
Fiduciary shall not instruct Processor to process in violation of the Act.
5. Cross-border transfers
Processor shall not transfer Personal Data outside India except to destinations not restricted under Section 16 and with Fiduciary's written approval.
6. Liability
Processor indemnifies Fiduciary for losses arising from Processor's breach of this DPA, subject to liability caps in the Master Agreement except where prohibited by the Act.
7. Governing law
Governed by laws of India. Courts at Mumbai, Maharashtra have exclusive jurisdiction.
8. Audit rights
Fiduciary may audit once per year on thirty (30) days' notice, or accept Processor's annual SOC 2 Type II report.

For CloudHost Technologies India Pvt. Ltd.: _________________________  Date: ____/____/____

Recitals
The Customer engages the Vendor to provide payroll, TDS, provident fund and employee state insurance processing services.
In providing such services, the Vendor processes personal data of the Customer's employees on the Customer's behalf.
The parties wish to document the Vendor's obligations as a Data Processor under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows:
1. Appointment and scope
Customer appoints Vendor as Data Processor to process employee personal data solely to deliver payroll, TDS, PF and ESI services under the Master Services Agreement dated 01 April 2025.
2. Processing instructions
Vendor shall process only per Customer's documented instructions, this DPA and applicable law.
If Vendor believes an instruction violates the Act, it shall promptly notify Customer.
3. Confidentiality
All personnel with access bound by confidentiality surviving termination by five (5) years.
4. Security schedule (Rule 6)

items: SOC 2 Type II certified payroll platform
Encryption of PAN and bank account data
Two-factor authentication for Customer administrators
Annual penetration test - summary shared on request
Disaster recovery tested semi-annually

sections.text: 5. Sub-processors

6. Audit
Customer may audit annually on thirty (30) days' notice or accept Vendor's SOC 2 report.
7. Breach notification
Vendor notifies Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of any personal data breach with details sufficient for Rule 7 compliance.
8. Deletion
Within thirty (30) days of MSA termination, Vendor deletes all personal data and certifies deletion. Backups roll off within ninety (90) days.
9. Indemnity
Vendor indemnifies Customer for regulatory fines and direct damages arising from Vendor's breach of this DPA.

Subject: Important security notice regarding your Acme account
Dear [Customer Name],

We are writing to inform you of a security incident involving limited personal data held by Acme Digital Solutions Private Limited ("Acme"). We take the protection of your information seriously and are committed to being transparent about what happened and what we are doing.
What happened

On 17 March 2026, our security team detected unauthorised access to a read-only API endpoint using a compromised integration key. The access occurred between approximately 16 March 11:40 PM and 17 March 8:50 AM IST. We immediately revoked the key, disabled the endpoint and began a forensic investigation with CrowdStrike.
What information was involved

The following data may have been accessed: your name, work email address, company name, subscription plan and last login date. Importantly, passwords (stored as bcrypt hashes), PAN, bank details and payment card data were NOT accessible through this endpoint.
What we are doing

items: Rotated all API keys and enforced MFA for administrative accounts
Engaged external forensic experts to confirm scope
Reported the incident to the Data Protection Board of India
Implemented additional WAF rules and anomaly detection
Offering free identity monitoring for 12 months via our partner

This Playbook establishes the mandatory incident response procedures of Acme Digital Solutions Private Limited for suspected or confirmed personal data breaches. It applies to all personnel, contractors and engaged processors.
Phase 1 - Detect and contain (0-12 hours)

items: Log incident in PagerDuty + Jira ticket ACME-SEC-____
Appoint Incident Commander (rotation: CISO → IT Director → On-call lead)
Isolate affected systems - disable accounts, revoke keys, block IPs, segment network
Preserve evidence - disk images, memory dumps, API logs, WAF logs (min 12 months per Rule 8(3))
Notify Legal, CCO and CEO within 1 hour for all confirmed personal data breaches
Engage forensic firm (CrowdStrike retainer) if production data involved
Do NOT delete logs or rebuild systems before forensic preservation
Brief customer support with holding statement only - no speculation

sections.text: Phase 2 - Assess (12-48 hours)

items: Confirm personal data (not just corporate confidential data) is in scope
Map data categories: identity, financial, health, biometric, children's data, etc.
Estimate number of affected Data Principals (exact count or justified range)
Determine attack vector, root cause and whether ongoing
Assess harm likelihood: identity theft, financial loss, discrimination, reputational harm
Review processor involvement - notify CloudHost, Razorpay etc. if their systems involved
Decision record: Board notification required? (Y/N with rationale)
Decision record: Principal notification required? (Y/N with rationale)
Legal reviews 72-hour deadline from time of awareness (not occurrence)

sections.text: Phase 3 - Notify (within 72 hours of awareness)

items: File Board notification via prescribed portal - use Breach Notice Part A template
CEO and Board briefed before external notification
Principal notification: email primary channel; SMS for critical incidents; website banner
Notification content: what happened, data involved, actions taken, principal steps, contact
Regulators in other jurisdictions if applicable (e.g. MAS for Singapore affiliate data)
Prepare FAQ for support team - route media to comms@acmedigital.in only
Do not admit liability beyond facts in legal-approved statements

sections.text: Phase 4 - Recover and learn (48 hours onwards)

items: Deploy remediation - patches, MFA enforcement, key rotation, access review
Monitor for recurrence 90 days - enhanced SOC rules
Post-incident review within 14 days: timeline, root cause, control gaps
Update RoPA, risk register, DPIA if processing changed
Board report within 30 days for material incidents
Staff training update if human error contributed
Insurance notification to cyber policy broker within policy timeframe

sections.text: Roles and contacts
Escalation to CEO immediately if

items: More than 10,000 Data Principals affected
Financial, health or children's data exposed
Ransomware with data exfiltration
Media inquiry or social media trending
Board notification deadline at risk (<12 hours remaining)
Law enforcement involvement
